title: A nested mapping added after 300 scalar entries copies the indentation of the first nested sibling
notes: The document has 300 scalar entries and then one entry, `x`, with nested content indented by four spaces at both depths (`y` is four spaces in, the sequence under `z` is eight). The added mapping is written in the style of its siblings: the only siblings that show how a nested collection is indented are the ones in `x`, so each level is four spaces in and `b` is eight. Reading the style from the first few hundred entries alone would find only scalars and fall back to two spaces. The existing cases edit/add-mapping-value-indent-four and edit/add-mapping-value-indent-two show the same rule with the nested sibling first. Copying the indentation of nested siblings and putting a new member at the end of its mapping are kit conventions (docs/edit-semantics.md).

provenance.reference: A writer that looked for the indentation of nested siblings only among the first 256 entries and wrote two spaces here.
